correctionAssessment.allocation: Immutable limits registration no longer starts lifetime. One MATERIALIZED claim_clock supplies the allocation's firstClaimAt and all computed deadlines. COALESCE preserves existing first claim and lifetime on reclaim; SQL computes execution/lease bounds from the stored limits. The allocation WHERE guards fence range, invocation cap, possible_dispatch=0 and remaining absolute lifetime at the allocation clock sample.
correctionAssessment.zeroRow: A reclaim reaching its immutable lifetime before allocation is rejected without a new fence/count charge. Fresh time and the stored ledger classify exhausted lifetime/cap as known-no-effect failed. An unexplained miss raises delivery.claim_allocation_rejected rather than authorizing a claim.
correctionAssessment.lateResult: After allocation and the running state statement settle, a fresh database time sample checks all returned deadlines. Late allocation returns null, retains the allocated fence/count, and becomes failed for lifetime/cap exhaustion or retry_wait when only lease/execution expired. No refund/reset or positive handle is issued in the reproduced slow-allocation/state paths.
correctionAssessment.preservedSafety: Per-key locking, FIFO, exact text fence handling, current-claim checkpoint conditions and possible-dispatch unknown priority remain intact. The unchanged live-token executor still guards each claim SQL callback. This correction adds no provider call or send authority.

retainedLimits: Approval resolves only the stale allocation-time finding in the private storage foundation. The original report's schema, host authority, worker, clock, provider and conformance limits remain applicable; whole RM-306 and the 18-case ASYNC catalog are not complete.

New ledgers require the compatible nullable first_claim_at/lifetime_deadline layout. An existing old v1 table with NOT NULL first-claim fields cannot accept the new limits-only insertion; CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS does not migrate or attest it. This approval assumes a fresh/compatible compiler-owned layout, not upgrade compatibility, schema collision handling or restored-record validation.

A database clock sample defines eligibility at that sample. Final clock-query response latency, further caller work, transaction commit delay and the later commit-to-dispatch interval can outlive a lease. No end-to-end wall-clock freshness or external dispatch permission is certified. Future worker binding must wait for commit acknowledgement, handle uncertainty and revalidate current fence/time at its checked effect boundary; positive checkpoint results inside an open transaction are provisional.

No provider dispatch, public/authored/operator/worker binding, renewal, receipt/acknowledgement, cancellation, scheduler, safe retry delay, dead-letter, attempt history or trusted resolution implementation certified.

The live token prevents new guarded SQL invocation after revocation, not hard interruption of already-running I/O or draining detached work. Generated operations must be awaited within their owning source/claim transaction. Unrelated persistence capabilities and concurrent arbitrary host callbacks remain outside this approval.

Missing backend, incompatible/corrupt schema, foreign-key/key assumptions, UUID collisions, payload limits, supported calendar/range boundaries, database-clock regressions, host/default clock semantics and concrete golden timeout/lease values remain their owning gates.

Main's fresh supported-gate completion is still separate evidence. No compiler build, broad gate, main execution-session polling, source/docs edit or whole-task closure was performed by this reviewer. Re-review substantive changes to the pinned correction bytes.
